data_governance_declaration: Track 2 pipeline-readiness rehearsal: synthetic corpus, replayed model calls, no human subjects, no external data-governance obligations.
exclusion_criteria: Studies not involving rural healthcare systems
Studies not using MBSE or computer simulation approaches
Studies not related to disaster preparedness or response

criteria.eligibility_requirement: The study applies computer simulation or model-based systems engineering (MBSE) methods (discrete-event, agent-based, or system-dynamics simulation, or systems modelling) to a disaster-planning problem.
The study concerns rural healthcare systems, rural healthcare facilities, or rural communities' healthcare, in a disaster context.
The study addresses disaster preparedness, planning, or response (natural disaster, pandemic, epidemic, or mass-casualty event).

funding_statement: This pipeline-readiness rehearsal received no external funding.
inclusion_criteria: Studies addressing computer simulation or MBSE approaches applied to disaster preparedness or response
Studies focused on rural healthcare systems or rural healthcare settings
Studies relevant to disaster planning, preparedness, or response
pcc_concept: Application of model-based systems engineering (MBSE), including computer simulation and systems thinking, to rural healthcare disaster planning
pcc_context: Disaster preparedness and response planning in rural healthcare settings
pcc_population: Rural healthcare systems and rural communities involved in disaster preparedness and response
research_questions: What is the current body of evidence on the application of computer simulation based on model-based systems engineering approaches to disaster preparedness and response for rural healthcare systems?
What MBSE methods, healthcare settings, disaster types, and contexts have been studied in rural healthcare disaster planning?
review_rationale: This run rehearses the chapter's end-to-end scoping-review automation pipeline on a synthetic corpus with replayed model calls, to demonstrate that every methodological artifact the chapter cites is produced and internally consistent before the audited Track-3 run on real data.
review_title: Pipeline-readiness rehearsal: MBSE and computer-simulation methods for rural healthcare disaster preparedness (scoping review)
seed_query: ((rural OR non-urban OR frontier) AND (healthcare OR "health care") AND (disaster OR pandemic OR epidemic) AND (simulation OR "agent based model" OR "system dynamics" OR "machine learning" OR "artificial intelligence"))
